Q: Writing specific sections from txt file to dataframe A:

you can use regex for matching pattern of dialouges and then you can trim them i wrote a little bit messy code for instance

import re
text = """Description Q. What should I do to get glowing fair skin?
        
Dialogue 
Patient: Hi doctor, My face and body color are different. My face is getting dark and black day-by-day. What should I do to increase my fairness and get glowing skin? Shall I use some night cream? 
Doctor: Hi. I have read your problem carefully. What is your nature of work? Will you get exposed to sunlight? ... Take care. 
    
id=13585 https://www.icliniq.com/qa/migraine-headaches/how-can-i-cure-one-sided-headache-with-vomiting
    
Description Q. How can I cure one sided headache with vomiting?
    
Dialogue
Patient: Hi doctor, I have one side headache. How to cure it? Will you please give your suggestion? During maigrane headache, I have vomiting. 
Doctor: Hello. You seem to be suffering from migraine.   
    
id=13586 https://www.icliniq.com/qa/diarrhea/what-is-causing-diarrhea-after-eating-a-spicy-dish"""

matchespatient = re.finditer("Patient: (.*?)\n", text, re.DOTALL)
matchesdoctor = re.finditer("Doctor: (.*?)\n", text, re.DOTALL)

zip_object = zip(matchespatient, matchesdoctor)
cnt = 0

print("\tPatient\t\t\t\t\t\t\tDoctor")
for i,j in zip_object:
    pat = i.group(0)[9:-1]
    doc = j.group(0)[8:-1]
    print(f"{cnt}\t{pat[:46]}...\t{doc[:46]}...")
    cnt+=1

Q: Best ways to concatinate strings in python A:

A couple of patterns that jump out at me scanning this:

total_element = len(parameter_list)
for i in range(total_element):
    parameter_value_str = f"{parameter_list[i]:.2f}"
    ...

If you're going to iterate through a list (or other iterable), use for parameter in parameter_list; don't go to integer indices and back.

image_name = ""
for parameter in parameter_list
    image_name += f"...,"
if image_name[-1] == ",":
    image_name = image_name[:-1]

Given a separator and a list, str.join() can create a string with the separator between each element but not one at the end.

I'd restructure this by computing each part separately. Where you have the comma-separated list of parts, I'd construct those parts with a list comprehension. I wouldn't append strings midway through, but use a single f-string at the end to compute the final result.

def create_title_from_parameters(
  parameter_list: list[float],
  function_name: str,
  current_image_name: str
) -> str:
  # (I'd also consider pathlib.Path methods here)
  original_image_name, extension = current_image_name.rsplit(".", 1)
  shortened_function_name = function_name.split("_", 1)[0]
  parameters = ",".join(f"{p:.2f}" for p in parameter_list)

  return f"{original_image_name}_{shortened_function_name}_{parameters}.{extension}"

more efficient

To a first approximation, string computation is free, even in an interpreted language like Python. You don't have any particular algorithmic-complexity concerns, and you're not doing network or file I/O. I wouldn't go out of my way to try to make this faster, unless you're really sure a profiler has pointed you at this as the critical path.

Q: VSTS terminology and structure A:

For a small team managing multiple independent applications, a good approach is to create a single Azure DevOps project and organize teams based on each application. This allows you to manage permissions and visibility at the team level, while keeping everything within one project for easier cross-application coordination.

Yes, each team can have its own repository—so you can have separate Git repos for each application—and they can also define their own build and release pipelines tailored to their specific needs, such as development, staging, and production environments.

Using area paths and security permissions effectively, you can ensure that teams only see and manage the work items relevant to their applications, while still sharing code repositories and build definitions where appropriate.

For a comprehensive guide on structuring Azure DevOps projects, teams, and security, see my article: ADO Project Structure
